title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. Grothendieck is classifying 'surfaces conformes' (Riemann surfaces, possibly non-orientable or bordered, i.e. dianalytic/Klein surfaces) by whether they admit a distinguished metric. The previous page found a unique distinguished metric except in a few exceptional cases. This page isolates which surfaces are hyperbolic.

Corollaire 3. Let X' be a connected Riemann surface (the manuscript's '0-connexe' means connected) and X ⊂ X' a connected open subset. Then X is hyperbolic (universal cover ≅ upper half-plane H) except in the following cases.
(a) X' ≅ P^1_C, resp. the affine line (written E^1_C), resp. G_m,C = C*, and the complement X'∖X has at most 2 points, resp. at most 1 point, resp. 0 points. These exceptional X are exactly P^1, C and C*.
(b) X' is compact of genus 1 and X = X'.
Proof idea (implicit): the non-hyperbolic connected Riemann surfaces are exactly P^1, C, C* and complex tori (uniformization). An open subset of a hyperbolic surface is hyperbolic. A domain in P^1 whose complement has at least 3 points is hyperbolic (little Picard / uniformization). A proper open subset of a torus is hyperbolic.

Remarque. Let X be a connected conformal surface, not necessarily orientable. Call X hyperbolic if its universal cover is ≅ H. Equivalently, every conformal map C → X is constant. A marginal note adds: equivalently, the orientation double cover is hyperbolic.
Thus the connected non-hyperbolic conformal surfaces without boundary are:
- the four orientable cases listed earlier: P^1, C, C*, tori;
- quotients of these by fixed-point-free anti-holomorphic involutions.
The page breaks off at 'On trouve donc de plus'. The expected list is:
- the real projective plane P^1/(z ↦ -1/z̄);
- the open Möbius band C*/(z ↦ -1/z̄);
- Klein bottles (quotients of tori).
C contributes nothing, since every antiholomorphic involution of C has a fixed line.
The aim is to set up the hyperbolic-versus-exceptional dichotomy for the canonical (curvature −1) metric used in the 'surgery of conformal surfaces' project.
errors: The written 'card(X∖X')' must be read as card(X'∖X), since X ⊂ X'. This is a slip, or a transcription issue.
Minor: in (a) the hypothesis that X is connected is needed and is implicitly assumed.
The Remark is restricted to surfaces without boundary ('ss bord', added above the line). Bordered cases such as the disc and the half-plane were treated separately on the previous page.

ideas.what: Classification of non-hyperbolic open subsets of Riemann surfaces: only P^1 minus at most 2 points, C minus at most 1 point, C*, and the whole torus
ideas.modern_name: Uniformization theorem / little Picard theorem; classification of non-hyperbolic Riemann surfaces

ideas.what: Hyperbolicity of non-orientable conformal (dianalytic) surfaces via the orientation double cover; the non-hyperbolic ones are quotients by fixed-point-free anti-involutions (RP^2, open Möbius band, Klein bottles)
ideas.modern_name: Klein surfaces / dianalytic structures; Brody-type hyperbolicity criterion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Klein; Alling–Greenleaf (1971) for the foundations of Klein surfaces
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions non-orientable and bordered surfaces in the context of dessins / the Teichmüller tower, but not this list

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard consequences of uniformization, extended in a routine way to non-orientable surfaces. They are of interest only as part of Grothendieck's systematic set-up of 'surgery of conformal surfaces' with canonical metrics.
transcription_corrections: 'o-convexe' / 'o-connexe' should read '0-connexe', Grothendieck's term for connected (also in 'ouvert 0-connexe' under X ⊂ X').
E^1_C denotes the complex affine line (affine space of dimension 1), not an elliptic curve.
The page number at the top appears to be (19), between pages (18) and (21).
The marginal note reads approximately: 'i.e. si encore le revêtement des orientations est une surface hyperbolique (i.e. que son revêtement universel est hyperbolique)'.
'dans (i) ci-dessus' probably refers to item (1) of the preceding summary of four cases.
